chunks: Muhammad ibn Ali Majilawayh (may Allah be pleased with him) narrated to us, saying: My uncle Muhammad ibn Abi al-Qasim narrated to us, saying: Harun ibn Muslim narrated to us, from Mas'ada ibn Ziyad, from al-Sadiq, Ja'far ibn Muhammad (peace be upon them both), from his father, from his forefathers (peace be upon them), who said: Ali (peace be upon him) said:

Indeed, a Muslim man has three close friends: one friend who says to him, 'I am with you alive and dead,' and that is his deed; one friend who says to him, 'I am with you until you die,' and that is his wealth, and when he dies it becomes for the heirs; and one friend who says to him, 'I am with you until the gate of your grave, then I leave you,' and that is his child.
ai.seo_question: What are the three close friends of a Muslim according to Imam Ali?
ai.summary: In *Mani al-Akhbar*, Shaykh al-Saduq records this profound narration from Imam al-Sadiq (peace be upon him) tracing back to Imam Ali (peace be upon him), categorizing the 'friends' of a human being by their duration of companionship. While wealth and offspring are temporary companions that eventually depart or are inherited, righteous deeds are the only true friend that accompanies the believer from life through death and into the grave, emphasizing the Shia emphasis on *amal* (action) as the enduring legacy of the soul.
